hints: Focus on counting all shared pairs as bond pairs and all non-bonding pairs as lone pairs across the whole species.
Start with ammonia, $\text{NH}_3$, which has three N-H bonds and one lone pair on nitrogen, then see what changes when it becomes $\text{NH}_4^+$.
Remember a dative bond still counts as a bond pair, so check which species has used up its lone pair to make an extra bond.
walkthrough:
**Recall what to count**

A bond pair is any shared pair, including each pair in a multiple bond. A lone pair is a non-bonding pair on any atom in the species. We must count totals for the whole species.

Rule:
$$\text{total valence pairs = bond pairs + lone pairs}$$

**Check nitrogen and ammonia**

Nitrogen molecule, $\text{N}\equiv\text{N}$, has a triple bond so 3 bond pairs. Each N keeps one lone pair, so total lone pairs = 2, not 1.

Ammonia, $\text{NH}_3$, has three N-H single bonds so 3 bond pairs, plus 1 lone pair on N.

**Check ammonium and hydroxide**

Ammonium ion, $\text{NH}_4^+$, is formed when $\text{NH}_3$ uses its lone pair to bond to $\text{H}^+$. That gives 4 N-H bond pairs and 0 lone pairs.

Hydroxide ion, $\text{OH}^-$, has one O-H bond so 1 bond pair. Oxygen has 3 lone pairs to complete its octet, so total lone pairs = 3, not 4.

**Pick the correct row**

Only the ammonium ion row matches 4 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs, so that row is correct.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{N}_2$ does have 3 bond pairs from the triple bond, but each nitrogen atom has 1 lone pair, giving 2 lone pairs in total, not 1.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{NH}_3$ has only 3 N-H bond pairs, not 4. The 1 lone pair value is correct, but students often miscount total pairs around N as 4 and call them all bond pairs.
options.C: Correct. $\text{NH}_4^+$ has four N-H bonds, including one dative bond formed using the lone pair from $\text{NH}_3$. So there are 4 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs left.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{OH}^-$ has 1 bond pair, which is correct, but oxygen has only 3 lone pairs. The extra negative charge gives one extra electron to make 3 pairs, not 4 pairs. Counting 4 lone pairs would give oxygen 9 valence electrons.
